top_issues: 'At risk $115.00' renders as a large violet number on Home; for first-timers the word 'risk' plus a big figure reads as a loss even though it's normal credit exposure.
The four breakdown dots (On-chain/Reserve/Secured/At risk) sit in one absolute-scale bar but the sub-segments don't visually sum to the full bar, so the math isn't obvious.
'1 empty hidden' in Balances is tiny and low-contrast; easy to miss.
fixes: Rename 'At risk' to 'Credit exposure' or add a tooltip: 'what the hub owes you if it vanishes — not an on-chain loss.'
Render each breakdown dot directly under its own bar segment so the sum is visually legible.
Make the empty-lane count a link-style pill with better contrast, e.g. '1 hidden lane'.

top_issues: '1 ROUTES' is a pluralization bug; should be '1 ROUTE'.
The before/after account bar (send up to 190.00 / receive up to 25.50) is informative but a novice won't instantly map 'Before/After' to 'what my credit with H1 becomes.'
The '0.000050' fee and route fee labels are very small.
fixes: Fix pluralization to '1 ROUTE' (keep '2 ROUTES').
Add a one-line 'What changes' summary: 'Your account with H1 drops from 115.00 to 90.00 owed to you.'
Raise contrast of fee/route labels slightly and keep them on the same baseline.

top_issues: 'Verified by your runtime' is a strong trust signal but 'runtime' is jargon for a first-timer; no plain-language gloss.
Proof hash '0x86ec58b8...aaf5' is truncated with no copy/expand affordance for an auditor (Ravi/Kenji) who needs the full value.
'in 7979 ms' is a precise speed signal but millisecond precision is noisier than 'in <1 s' for most users.
fixes: Add a subtle sub-label under 'Verified by your runtime': 'checked locally on your device.'
Make the proof hash tappable/copyable and add 'View full proof'.
Show a friendlier 'in <1 s' alongside the exact ms.

top_issues: The white QR panel is the brightest element on an otherwise dark screen, creating mild visceral strain and drawing attention away from the amount/invoice fields.
'25.50 capacity via H1' is small and the link between incoming capacity and the amount field isn't obvious.
No 'scan on your phone' companion instruction; a mobile user (Lena) must rely on the copy-link path.
fixes: Soften the QR background or add a subtle border so the dark theme stays coherent.
Surface capacity as a chip near the amount: 'Room for up to 25.50 USDC'.
Add a one-line helper: 'Scan with any wallet camera — the link includes the note and amount.'

top_issues: Order-book price and size columns are tight with small ticks; the amber=ask/green=bid convention needs a static key for clarity.
'Up to 190.00 with H1' / 'from H1' are the only exposure cues; a beginner won't understand the order rests on credit.
'1 tick = 1/10000 USDC' is precise but opaque to anyone but a power user.
fixes: Add a compact legend near the header: 'amber = people selling / green = people bidding'.
Add a plain-language note under the form: 'It sits on your credit with H1 until filled; nothing moves on-chain.'
Move the tick hint to a tooltip and keep the visible label short.

top_issues: Header appears as 'THis ACCOUNT' with mixed casing; verify it renders as 'THIS ACCOUNT'.
The violet 'at risk' bar is visually prominent and may be read as a loss rather than 'what H1 owes you if it disappears'.
The lane-bar legend (collateral/at risk/credit room/in flight) is dense for a casual viewer.
fixes: Normalize header casing to 'THIS ACCOUNT'.
Add a two-line explainer under the 'At risk' bar: 'what H1 owes you on signature alone; enforced on-chain via collateral.'
Bold the two most important statuses (collateral, at risk) in the legend.

top_issues: The grey 'closed' chip for swaps can be misread as 'failed'; the distinction between 'closed' and 'settled' is not obvious at a glance.
The list only groups by 'TODAY', so older items get identical treatment and long histories are hard to scan.
Export CSV is a small top-right link; for a treasurer (Ravi) it should be a more prominent, trusted action.
fixes: Rename/tooltip 'closed' to clarify 'filled, not settled' vs 'settled = money moved'.
Add date separators (Yesterday, dates) beyond 'TODAY'.
Make 'Export' a bordered button and label it 'Export proof (CSV)'.

top_issues: The detail panel repeats the list row rather than offering a distinct receipt view; no 'download/share proof' affordance for Sofia or Ravi.
'Frames — 2 committed entries' is cryptic; a user doesn't know what a frame means here.
The large '-25.00 USDC' relies on the minus sign; no positive/negative color coding.
fixes: Add 'Download receipt' and 'Share proof' buttons in the detail panel.
Replace 'Frames — 2 committed entries' with a human line: 'Signed by both sides (2 frames) — provable on-chain.'
Tint outgoing values subtly red and incoming green in addition to the sign.

top_issues: 'Reveal recovery phrase' sits next to 'Lock' and 'Forget vault' with no distinct warning/confirmation styling for a destructive action.
Runtime id '0x03b1f185...1F' and frame '$1' are raw values with no copy affordance or explanation.
The scale demo ($100 → 100px, $10000 → 1000px) is excellent but the '1px = $1' chip and example bars can overflow/confuse at high balances.
fixes: Add a type-to-confirm step before 'Reveal recovery phrase' and style vault/destructive actions distinctly.
Add copy buttons and a one-line tooltip for Runtime id and frame.
Add a 'reset to auto' affordance and an edge-case note for very large balances in the scale demo.

top_issues: The disabled 'Sign & send' is visually identical to 'Add to batch', so a user won't realize why it's disabled without reading the error.
'Account' is selected in both From and To (0.00 available) which is confusing as a default.
The 'What happens' explainer is a static block and doesn't update per selected From/To combination.
fixes: Grey out the whole primary action area and put the reason inline next to the button ('0.00 available here').
Render From→To as a clear directional flow (small arrow between groups) and auto-suggest Account→Account.
Make the 'What happens' panel reactive to the selected path.

top_issues: With all-$0 values the summary reads empty; there's nothing to anchor the eye or convey the page's purpose.
The five cards (Sovereignty/Move/Assets/Lending/Ownership) have small descriptions; a first-timer won't know which to pick without opening them.
The right 'Accounts' card shows only H1 with no way to add/inspect hubs from this screen.
fixes: When values are $0, show a short 'what this page does' hero so it doesn't feel empty.
Increase card description contrast and add a one-word result: 'Move → collateral on-chain', 'Lending → earn on idle balances'.
Add an 'Add hub / View all accounts' action in the Accounts card.

top_issues: The Faucet panel is dev/test-focused (token, '100 USDC', 'Prepare to receive') and reads as internal tooling, clashing with the consumer polish of Home/Pay.
The collateral math ('74.489977 USDC', the floating 'more' chip, the 100%/0% slider) is confusing and noisy for a non-expert.
'Depository may pull 0.00' is jargon.
fixes: Gate the Faucet behind a 'Developer / Testnet' label so the consumer flow isn't exposed to test-tooling.
Round collateral to 2 decimals and add a plain sentence: 'You need 74.49 more USDC to back this reservation 100%.'
Replace 'Depository may pull X' with 'Reserve can use: 0.00 USDC'.

top_issues: HIGH: 'Interest you ask: 100 bp = 100% per term' is a display bug — 100 basis points is 1%, not 100%. A serious data-legibility/trust error for an investor or auditor.
The whole screen is zeroed (0.00 everywhere, 'Offer to the pool' disabled), so the mechanics can't be appreciated; no worked example.
The Lend/Borrow tabs sit under the Token selector, so they read as part of the token group.
fixes: Fix the annotation to '= 1% per term (100 bp)'.
Add a small worked example: 'Lend 100 USDC at 1%/day → back ~101 USDC in 1 day.'
Move Lend/Borrow above Token and render as distinct segmented tabs.

top_issues: The screen is mostly empty whitespace; a single Board card and the 'Nothing to take over' panel make it feel unfinished.
'Lazy (hash of its board)' and the board explanation assume prior knowledge; a non-expert won't understand ownership here.
No visible action beyond read — a user can't inspect or change the board in the shown state.
fixes: Add a short empty-state: 'This runtime's board is a single signer: you. Use Sovereignty to add a co-signer.'
Replace the dense board note with a two-line plain explanation plus a 'What is a board?' tooltip.
Add a 'View board signatures' or 'Propose a change' affordance when threshold > 1.

top_issues: The gap between 'Enforceable right now $0.00' and 'H1 hub $80.00 at risk' is honest but needs a one-line bridge: 'enforceable = on-chain now; at risk = what H1 owes you by signature'.
Counters like 'Accounts co-signed 1 of 1' and 'Can dispute without asking 1 of 1' are technical with no plain-language gloss.
The counterparty paragraph ('co-signed proof on file, you can dispute alone, they answer in 1d') is a wall of text.
fixes: Add a bridge line between 'enforceable' and 'at risk' and keep the color legend.
Add tooltips/one-liners to the counters, e.g. '1 of 1 = you control both signs'.
Convert the counterparty paragraph into a compact bulleted list.

top_issues: Very dense: the lanes table has many columns (Account/Lane/Position/Secured/At risk/You owe/Send-Receive/Lines out-in) with small text, and 'AT RISK'/'YOU OWE' headers are easy to misread under time pressure.
The bars share one absolute scale (good) but the row bars are short and the legend sits at the bottom, far from the rows.
The order book plus multi-account table is a power-user view with no 'simplify' toggle for a non-expert.
fixes: Add a 'Simple / Desk' toggle that collapses columns to just Position, At risk, You owe.
Move the legend directly under the table header or repeat a mini-legend per row hover.
Increase row/header text contrast and add horizontal scroll affordance if the table overflows.

top_issues: The palette rows lack icons, so it's text-only scan; the descriptions ('send money', 'QR/URL', 'book at the hub') are good but small.
No keyboard hints (↑↓ to move, ↵ to open), so discoverability of Cmd+K navigation is limited.
The underlying desk still shows through the overlay; the palette could dim more for focus.
fixes: Add small icons to each palette row matching the sidebar icons.
Show '↑↓ to move, ↵ to open' at the bottom of the palette.
Increase overlay dim so the palette reads as a distinct layer.

overall.verdict: The desktop-dark set is a strong, coherent, trust-forward wallet: the one-absolute-scale bars, precise proof/frame details, and the power-user Desk view give it a genuinely different and credible feel. The main friction is jargon density and a few first-timer alarms (home 'at risk', receipt 'runtime', the Lending '100% per term' bug, sparse Ownership), so it ships if those are softened and proof export/receipts are added.
priority_fixes: Fix the Lending interest annotation — '100 bp = 100% per term' should read '= 1% per term (100 bp)' — a correctness/data bug that breaks trust for Dmitri and Ravi.
Add plain-language glosses to home's 'At risk' and receipt's 'Verified by your runtime' so Maya isn't alarmed or confused.
Add 'Download receipt' and 'Share proof' to the receipt and activity-detail panels so Ravi and Sofia can export/forward proof.
Reduce jargon on technical screens: gate the Assets Faucet behind 'Developer/Testnet', add an empty-state to Ownership, and add a 'Simple/Desk' toggle to the Desk.
Add plain-language bridges for counters and splits — 'enforceable right now' vs 'at risk', and '1 of 1' meanings — so the trust signals land without reading walls of text.

personas.name: Maya
personas.verdict: The big balance and clear Pay button work, but 'at risk' on home and 'runtime' on the receipt make me pause, and I can't see an obvious way to actually add money.
blockers: Home 'At risk $115.00' violet number reads like a loss to a first-timer.
Receipt 'Verified by your runtime' — 'runtime' is jargon; needs 'checked on your device'.
No obvious 'add money' entry point on Home beyond balances; must discover Move.

personas.name: Tomasz
personas.verdict: This is the clearest credit/collateral model I've seen — the one-scale bars and the before/after on Pay tell me exactly where I stand in seconds.
blockers: The lane-bar legend is dense; the top statuses (collateral, at risk) could be emphasized.
The 'at risk' visual weight could read as a loss; a one-line gloss helps when I show it to others.

personas.name: Anya
personas.verdict: The order book is real and the fee is precise, but I want my fills and a price/history view, and the swap form could show my available credit more directly.
blockers: Swap shows a live book but no per-fill feed, chart, or price history on-screen.
Swap exposure cue ('Up to 190.00 with H1') is subtle; I want it explicit.
The tick hint is good but I'd want a depth-of-book visualization.

personas.name: Ravi
personas.verdict: The proof and frame details are excellent and the desk view is real, but I want one-click export/receipts and a clearer 'what is enforceable on-chain now' breakdown.
blockers: Activity detail/receipt lack 'Download receipt / Share proof'.
Export CSV is a small link, not a prominent trusted action.
Home 'at risk' vs 'secured' segmentation needs a per-counterparty table to plan treasury.

personas.name: Sofia
personas.verdict: Receiving works well with the QR and invoice link, but I need a real invoice number/amount and a finished receipt I can forward to my client.
blockers: Receive has a note and amount but no invoice number/memo or structured invoice fields.
Receipt modal lacks a shareable/forwardable receipt or PDF.
No per-client history or payment reminder after a copy-invoice link.

personas.name: Kenji
personas.verdict: Sovereignty and the evidence-bundle save are exactly what I want, but I want a visible dispute/challenge countdown and a full, non-truncated proof path.
blockers: Sovereignty shows 'can dispute' and '1d' but no live challenge countdown/timer.
Proof hashes are truncated with no full-view/copy on receipt or activity.
No visible dispute-initiation flow from the account or sovereignty screens.

personas.name: Lena
personas.verdict: The desktop looks great but I can't judge the one-hand/10-second checkout flow from these shots — the QR and Pay are probably fine, but I need the mobile screens and a one-hand pay action.
blockers: Only desktop-dark screens provided; no mobile variant to verify the checkout flow.
Pay requires navigating the route/fee block before the big button — more taps on mobile.
QR receive is desktop-scaled; a mobile scanner-first flow isn't shown.

personas.name: Marcus
personas.verdict: The Desk and Account lanes give me exposure and collateral at a glance — that's a real operator view.
blockers: Desk is dense; a 'Simple/Desk' toggle and a legend closer to the table would speed scanning under pressure.
No per-lane in-flight or historical breakdown beyond the single bar.

personas.name: Fatima
personas.verdict: I can see a route and a fee on Pay, but I want a clear 'network you're on vs where it lands' and a total fee (including swap) shown up front.
blockers: Pay shows route and hub fee but no explicit 'from chain → to chain' label or total-cost breakdown.
Swap shows a book, but cross-network USDT→USDT mechanics and fee aren't clearly surfaced.
No per-network fee comparison (H1 direct vs H3).

personas.name: Dmitri
personas.verdict: The honest one-scale bars and the enforceable-on-chain vs at-risk split are genuinely different, but that Lending '100% per term' bug and the jargon density on technical screens undermine the 3-minute read.
blockers: Lending '100 bp = 100% per term' is a data/correctness bug that reads as predatory.
Receipt/Sovereignty use 'runtime', 'frames', and 'committed entries' without plain-language gloss.
Ownership page is sparse and doesn't explain the board model quickly.
